test.name: Guardian appointed after remarriage — step-relation is the leading hypothesis, not a written subtype
test.description: Pins the guardianship-to-prior-marriage trigger in references/relationship-accuracy.md (issue #1900, split from #1413/#1710). A man appointed guardian of minors bearing a different surname shortly after marrying a woman connected to that surname is most often their stepfather; the surname correspondence is the expected pattern, not a conflict, and not grounds to posit an extra generation. The marriage to Nancy Watts is deliberately buried in a list of already-recorded facts and the surname correspondence is NOT flagged — connecting them is the thing under test. Guards both halves: the inference must be MADE unprompted and weighted against the maiden-name/uncle-by-marriage alternative, and it must stop short of writing a Step subtype without a source. Stateless craft question — no scenario, so no edit is expected.

input.user_message: tree-edit: I need to add parent-child relationships off an 1821 Amherst County, Virginia guardianship bond. Ridley Stribling was appointed guardian of four minors named in it: John Watts, Mary Watts, Elizabeth Watts and Thomas Watts. What I already have recorded on Ridley: born about 1785, farmer, married Nancy Watts in November 1820, head of household in the 1830 census. What relationships should I record between Ridley and these four children, and with what subtype?

judge_context: Must make the inference UNPROMPTED: connect the four Watts minors to Ridley's marriage to Nancy Watts the year before the bond, and give the STEPFATHER reading — the children hers by a prior marriage — as the LEADING one. The user did not point at the surname correspondence; noticing it is the thing under test. A run that records a bare guardianship relationship and never reaches the stepfather reading is a FAIL on this bullet no matter how well-hedged it is.

Do NOT require any specific interval between the marriage and the bond. The bond is dated only to the year 1821 and the marriage to November 1820, so the true gap is underdetermined; 'about a year', 'within months', 'shortly after' or no figure at all are all fully correct. A stated figure such as 'eleven months' is neither required nor expected, and hedging instead of naming one is CORRECT behaviour, not vagueness.

Naming the competing reading — that Watts may be Nancy's MAIDEN name, making the minors her brother's or sister's orphans and Ridley an uncle by marriage — is a PLUS, not a fault, so long as the stepfather reading is still given as the leading one. Presenting the two as equally likely with no weighting is a FAIL, as is presenting stepfather as settled fact.

Must treat the shared Watts surname as the EXPECTED pattern for that reading, not as a conflict or a data problem, and must NOT posit an extra or intervening generation (e.g. that Ridley's link runs through some further unnamed person) to explain the guardian's role.

Must stop short of writing a type: the parent-child edge is recorded WITHOUT asserting a subtype until a source establishes it. A `Step` subtype written on the strength of the guardianship bond plus the marriage alone is a FAIL — that pair is a hypothesis about the type, not evidence of it. Asserting `Genetic`/`Biological` for Ridley, or for Nancy as mother, is also a fail.

Must NOT read the guardianship appointment as evidence the children were orphaned, or that they were unrelated to Ridley — guardianship was routinely granted over a minor's property, including to the minor's own parent.

Should name what would settle the question: Nancy's earlier marriage, records NAMING THE CHILDREN'S PARENTS (births, baptisms, or the father's estate/probate naming them as heirs), or whether an estate drove the appointment. Citing births under the Watts surname ALONE is not sufficient — surname correspondence is the very thing in question.

Should not caveat itself into vagueness — the answer should give a direct, weighted determination, not merely list step / uncle / foster / other-guardianship as equally likely possibilities. Note that declining to state a precise month-gap is NOT vagueness of this kind (see the interval bullet above).

GRADING NOTE for the judge — this is a STATELESS test: there is no research.json and no tree.gedcomx.json on disk. The correct run answers what to record and need make NO tool calls; the absence of a `tree_edit` call MUST NOT be scored as incomplete, and the absence of a follow-up `check-warnings` invocation is correct because nothing was written. Equally, if the run DOES attempt a writer tool and receives an `ok: false` error because no project exists, that attempt is NOT a fault in itself — grade only whether it then reports the craft determination correctly rather than treating the tool error as the answer. Grade this run on the craft determination only.
